techniques.name: stepped push into a halftone crowd
techniques.description: A grid of about 14x10 portrait tiles in blue halftone appears at 18% of frame width on white (F1) and scales up past the frame edges in four frames (F1-F5), then the push decays over about 0.6 s (diff 49 at F5-F6 to 11 at F23). A second, smaller step jumps at F48 (1.600) and settles by about F64. The search overlay stays fixed in size and place while the grid moves.
techniques.routeReason: Flat grid of images scaled by a frame-driven track; two keyed steps. The halftone itself is not in the library: missing:halftone-treatment must render any photo as round dots on a fixed screen grid with dot size from luminance, a two-colour palette and per-frame seeded flicker. The second step is the snap-zoom block's jump-and-settle on a still grid.

ease.name: expo.out
evidence: visuals/a1/open-grid-zoom.jpg diffs 2.5, 4.2, 5.9, 29.8, 49.4, 49.4, 47.1, 44.1 ... 11.0 (F1-F23): a 4-frame ramp then a long exponential tail
motion.json s002/s003 fits rejected: their spans (0.728+1.557 s, 1.893+2.116 s) run past the shot ends

sound.note: Onsets at 0.093 and 0.186 s sit on the first step's ramp (F3-F6); the second step starts 21 ms after an onset at 1.579 s, in the sparse intro (1.8 onsets a second). What makes the onsets is inferred. Times are measured; the kind is a guess.

techniques.name: frosted search field typing over the crowd
techniques.description: A magnifier dot appears at frame centre (F10), stretches into a frosted translucent pill about 50% of frame width (F11-F19), and a long query types in from F22 at about one character a frame, finishing at about F78 (2.60). At F86-F87 the pill's outline brightens for two frames as a submit before the cut.
techniques.routeReason: The prompt-bar block covers a typing field; the frosted look needs a backdrop blur over the moving grid, and the pill must sit outside the camera so it does not scale.

techniques.name: crowd-to-one cut
techniques.description: Two-frame submit flash on the search pill (F86-F87), then a hard cut at F88 (2.933) to white with a one-frame ghost of the grid, and one tile from the crowd at about 9% of frame width at centre, growing to 24% width by F90 and then almost still.
techniques.routeReason: A cut plus a two-frame scale pop; the ghost frame is a one-frame cross-fade. Nothing missing beyond the halftone.

ease.name: expo.out
evidence: visuals/a1/grid-to-one.jpg tile width F88 about 9%, F89 about 17%, F90 about 24%, then near-still F90-F101 (diffs 5.9, 3.0, 2.7, 3.5 ...)

sound.note: A loudness swell peaks at 2.925 s, 8 ms before the cut; no onset nearer than 1.1 s. What the swell is, is inferred. Times are measured; the kind is a guess.

techniques.name: halftone resolves to photo with the name typing in
techniques.description: The tile's halftone dots flicker frame to frame while the name types below it (one glyph a frame with a short blur-in, F107-F119) and the section label begins typing at top right, slower (about one glyph every three frames). F120-F125 (4.0-4.167) the halftone cross-fades to the real photo, still slightly blue at F125; a small verified badge pops at F122.
techniques.routeReason: An opacity cross-fade between a halftone render and the photo, plus per-glyph typed text with blur. The flicker needs the seeded halftone primitive.

ease.name: sine.inOut
evidence: visuals/a1/push-to-summary.jpg diffs 0.99, 1.13, 1.15, 2.51, 2.77, 4.31 (F121-F126): the cross-fade speeds up towards its end

typography.entry: per-glyph blur-in typewriter, 1 glyph per frame

techniques.name: punch-in cut on a word still typing
techniques.description: F130 the section label has typed six letters with the seventh arriving (cap height 0.037 of frame height) at top right. F131 (4.367) hard-cuts to the word at hero size (cap height 0.165, about 4.4x), restarted two letters back (four letters, the fifth arriving) (word 57% of frame width when finished, left edge x 0.20), and typing continues: one more glyph about every two frames, each arriving blurred and sharpening over 2-3 frames; a light-grey body line types under it at about one glyph a frame.
techniques.routeReason: Two framings of one interface layer, switched on a frame, with a typing schedule each; the hero framing restarts about two letters behind the label, so the count steps back at the cut. The camera-read block or RegionCamera holds both framings of one stage; the one-frame re-set of typed text is block ui-prompt-bar's jumpAt (which keeps the count).

ease.name: steps(1)
evidence: visuals/a1/push-to-summary.jpg F130-F131 diff 26.45 on one frame, then 0.5

typography.role: hero section label and body line
typography.entry: per-glyph blur-in typewriter, about 2 frames per glyph (label), 1 frame per glyph (body)
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 4.517-5.017 box x 0.203 w 0.568 h 0.232

techniques.name: ui-punch-in-reframe: alternating-side reframes on one record
techniques.description: Three more hard cuts on the same record, each made while the camera is moving: F158 (5.267) from the hero label mid-pan to the empty label column with the card's shadow at left; F216 (7.2) from the label column mid-tilt to the value column with the card edge at right; F253 (8.433) from a value close-up to a wider crop holding both columns. The side of the card on screen alternates, so the eye starts each shot from the opposite edge.
techniques.routeReason: One rendered record on a stage, several RegionCamera framings switched on cut frames; the moves inside each framing continue across the cut. Real product interface required: capture or rebuild the real record (product-interface rule).

techniques.name: record rows fill as the camera tilts to meet them
techniques.description: In the label and value close-ups each row arrives just before the camera reaches it: the icon fades and scales in, then the label or value types at about one glyph a frame with a blur-in (e.g. a social row F180-F187, the next F185-F194). The view tilts down roughly half a frame height per shot on an in-out curve (motion.json otherMoves give 0.46, fitted across a cut), so a new row is always entering at the bottom third.
techniques.routeReason: Rows staggered against a camera keyed on the same frames; per-glyph typing. Must be the real interface (capture:app or the product's own components with test data).

evidence: visuals/a1/field-track.jpg F177-F200: tilt starts about F177 (5.9 s), speeds up to F191, still moving at the 7.2 cut
motion.json s005 otherMoves[1] (6.0 s, 1.31 s, y 0.456) straddles the corrected 7.2 cut because motion.json is fitted on detector shots; amount read as rough

typography.entry: icon fade-scale, then per-glyph blur-in typewriter

techniques.name: populate-then-pull-out-reveal
techniques.description: From the 8.433 reframe the camera pulls out about 3.5x in scale (the same value line is 0.444 of frame width at 7.5-8.0 s and 0.125 on the settled card; F253 is at close-up scale) until the whole record sits centred on white (about 46% x 90% of frame) with a soft shadow; strip diffs climb from 2.9 to a peak of 12.7 at F268 (8.93) and fall to 6.4 by F275, settling around 9.5 s. Held still to 11.067 (1.47 s).
techniques.routeReason: A RegionCamera pull-out on the same stage as the close-ups; the curve comes straight from the fit. Real record material required.

evidence: motion.json s005 camera startSec 8.433 durationSec 1.618 span90Sec 0.644 amount z -1.3765 trackedShare 0.93
scale check: speech-text.json screenText value line width 0.444 (7.517-8.017) vs 0.125 (9.017-11.017); motion.json z -1.38 (about 4x) slightly overstates it

ease.name: expo.inOut
evidence: motion.json s005 camera.ease gsap expo.inOut (rmse 0.006), bezier rmse 0.0008, pick bezier

techniques.name: hold the finished state before transforming it
techniques.description: Three deliberate rests: 1.47 s on the whole record after the pull-out, 0.47 s on the still card grid before the ripple, five empty white frames before the sign-off. Each precedes a change of state, so the change reads against a still image.

techniques.name: one becomes the crowd: cut and two-stage pull-out
techniques.description: Hard cut at F332 (11.067) from the full record to a grid of copies of that card in blue halftone (the opening's texture), three columns visible. Pull-out stage one: diffs ramp from 8 to 24.7 over F333-F340 and decay to about 2 by F357, while the halftone cross-fades to pale #C5D3ED cards over F341-F345. Stage two from F365 (12.16): immediate peak (16.8 at F366) and a long settle to F409 (13.63). Final grid about 14 columns at 64% of frame width.
techniques.routeReason: A grid of card renders with a track on scale; a halftone layer cross-faded out. Needs the halftone primitive for the first 0.4 s. The first-stage curve is read off the strip; the second uses the motion.json fit.

ease.name: circ.out
evidence: motion.json s006 camera startSec 12.127 durationSec 1.282 ease circ.out (gsap rmse 0.0119, bezier rmse 0.0074)
first stage from the strip: peak speed at about 25% of 1.07 s (F333-F364)

sound.note: The cut is 9 ms before an onset at 11.076 s and 58 ms before a swell at 11.125 s: the one measured sync point in the loud section. Beat and downbeat at 11.076 come from a grid of low confidence. Times are measured; the kind is a guess.

techniques.name: cards ripple into particles from the centre
techniques.description: From F424 (14.13) a ring of change spreads from the grid centre: each small card is replaced by a flat cobalt dot of one of three or four sizes, at its own grid position with a small jitter. By F447 (14.9) every card is a dot. The camera does not move.
techniques.routeReason: Per-cell switch timed by distance from centre, seeded size and jitter, drawn on a canvas or as SVG circles. The library's particle-assemble is a weak match (glowing points in a dark depth field, the opposite look): missing:grid-to-particle-field must swap each grid cell for a flat disc on a radial stagger and hand the discs to the stream that follows.

ease.name: power1.in
evidence: visuals/a1/grid-to-dots.jpg diffs 0.08, 0.07, 0.11, 0.13, 0.23, 0.24, 0.41 ... 0.63 (F424-F434): the ring widens faster as it grows

techniques.name: particle stream writes a two-part line
techniques.description: The dot field converges to a point at frame right, accelerating (F450-F461), then flattens into a band at mid-height that streams right and off frame (F462-F485). The first phrase types in at x 0.14 at the band's trailing edge (from F467); the second types inside the stream at x 0.67 as its tail exits (F493-F507). Both phrases sit on one baseline at y 0.50, small (about 4.7% of frame height).
techniques.routeReason: Particles on paths (seeded per-dot offsets, a shared flow towards a line), with type revealed behind the stream's tail. The camera fit at 15.4 s in motion.json (move_left, push_in, circ.in) is the dots converging, not a camera. missing:particle-stream-to-text must move a dot field along a converging flow into a band and expose glyphs where the band has passed.

typography.entry: typewriter at the particle stream's trailing edge
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 16.517-18.017 boxes x 0.144 and x 0.67, y 0.50

techniques.name: blur-fade through white to a baseline-matched sign-off
techniques.description: The two phrases blur and fade out together over F533-F539 (0.2 s); five frames of white; the product label blurs in at the left anchor (F545-F548) and the mark and wordmark at the right anchor (F546-F556), on the same baseline and x positions as the line they replace. Held about 0.9 s; everything blurs out over F584-F590 and the film ends on three white frames.
techniques.routeReason: Opacity with a filter blur keyed per element; the shared baseline is a layout decision.
